title: Customer Commitment Lifecycle: Negotiation Worksheet for Reserved GPU Tiers & Soft-Failover Policies
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Produce a single-page negotiation worksheet and decision checklist sales/PMs can use when intake teams evaluate enterprise reserved capacity requests. The artifact will standardize how we translate business requirements (SLOs, QPS/throughput, burst patterns) into a recommended reserved-throughput commitment, GPU family recommendation, pricing delta, and a soft-failover policy (what happens when reserved pool is saturated). The worksheet will include: 1) SLA target bands (p50/p95 latency thresholds, availability targets), 2) throughput-to-GPU mapping (example conversion tables for H100/A100/L4 by model size & sequence length), 3) burst/credit policy template and acceptable burst window, 4) preemption and fallback model variant ladder with canary rollout guidance, 5) pricing uplift calculator (simple formula: base hosted unit price * commitment factor * GPU multiplier + burst surcharge), 6) operational readiness checklist (metrics to monitor, required dashboards, alert thresholds, on-call playbook summary), 7) contract redlines and required telemetry clauses (token-level cost visibility, per-route SLOs), and 8) escalation matrix. Deliverables: a one-page PDF worksheet, a canonical Confluence page with worked examples, an internal PR template for account teams to attach on customer commit. This ticket coordinates PM + Sales + Solutions + Eng reliability to validate the conversion tables and runbook steps.
acceptance_criteria: One-page PDF negotiation worksheet populated with three worked examples (chat light, chat heavy, embeddings-heavy batch workload)
Confluence page published under /enterprise/capacity with conversion tables and the pricing calculator embedded
Two engineering sign-offs confirming GPU mapping and fallback ladder are feasible within current autoscaler constraints
Runbook checklist itemized and assigned owners for monitoring/alerts and canary rollout steps
Template PR for customer contract intake created and reviewed by Legal/RevenueOps
comments: 2026-02-28 | Asha Kapoor: Initial draft of worksheet outline attached. Focused on making an 'order-of-magnitude' conservative GPU-to-throughput table rather than precise micro-benchmarks to keep sales velocity high.

2026-03-02 | Diego Martínez: Shared with Solutions Eng. Requested examples for a latency-sensitive chat model (p95 200ms) and an embeddings batch job (throughput 2000 req/min). Asked ENG for mapping validation against current runtime-1.22 kernels.

2026-03-04 | Priya Nair (Solutions Eng): Verified H100 -> 10k tokens/min per GPU baseline for small-chat (context 1024) and noted degraded throughput for long-context (>4k). Recommended adding a note about sequence-length sensitivity and KV cache sizing.

2026-03-06 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Proposed operational alert thresholds: queue length >10% of pool, sustained token-RTT increase 20% over baseline, and error-rate >0.5%. Added requirement for a per-reservation dashboard template in Console.

2026-03-08 | Diego Martínez: Incorporated feedback; added soft-failover ladder (preferred model -> quantized variant -> fall back to lower-precision family -> degrade to safety-prompts). Drafted pricing uplift examples and attached spreadsheet (internal-only).

2026-03-10 | Legal (Anna Chen): Quick review: add clause requiring 30-day notice for GPU-family changes, and define objective metrics for SLA credit. Marked for final review once conversion tables locked.
decision_notes: Use conservative throughput estimates (25% headroom) to avoid overcommitment and frequent preemption incidents.
Default burst window = 5 min at up to 2x committed throughput; excess billed at burst surcharge unless pre-bought burst credits are attached.
Soft-failover ladder will be embedded in contract as an operational commitment; customers may opt-out for higher committed uplifts.
Require telemetry contract clause: Redwood must receive anonymized per-route token counts and p95 latency to validate SLO adherence.
